name: Anaplastic Ganglioglioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of both neoplastic ganglion cells and malignant glial components with anaplastic features
MRI showing a heterogeneously enhancing mass with cystic and solid components, often involving temporal lobe
Detection of BRAF V600E mutation or other relevant genetic alterations supporting diagnosis
Seizures or focal neurological deficits consistent with tumor location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of neoplastic ganglion cells with anaplastic glial features is mandatory; supportive imaging and molecular findings aid diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, imaging, and molecular data per WHO CNS tumor guidelines.

pathognomonic.notes: Often drug-resistant and presenting as the initial symptom
searchTerms: seizures starting in one area of brain

pathognomonic.notes: Depends on tumor location, commonly hemiparesis or aphasia
searchTerms: gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
common.notes: Often worse in the morning or with Valsalva maneuvers
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure

common.notes: May occur if tumor affects optic pathways
searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.notes: May include irritability or mood disturbances
searchTerms: behavioral changes or mental health issues

occasional.notes: Due to involvement of sensory cortex or pathways
searchTerms: numbness or tingling on one side
sensory loss in part of the body

rare.notes: Leads to worsening intracranial pressure symptoms
searchTerms: brain fluid buildup from tumor blockage
water accumulation in brain due to tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
rare.notes: Rare but possible if tumor extends to hypothalamic region
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion

rare.notes: If tumor invades brainstem or adjacent structures
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI with contrast showing mixed cystic and solid mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Peritumoral edema and mass effect common
genetic: Alterations in CDKN2A/B and TP53 genes in anaplastic components
other: Histopathology demonstrating neoplastic ganglion cells with malignant glial proliferation and increased mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry positive for neuronal markers (NeuN, synaptophysin) and glial markers (GFAP)

distinguishingFeatures: Pilocytic astrocytoma lacks neoplastic ganglion cells
Typically WHO Grade I with less aggressive behavior
Distinct imaging features with cyst and mural nodule
More rapid progression and necrosis on histology
Different molecular profile, often EGFR amplification
Lower mitotic index and absence of necrosis

redFlags: New onset of drug-resistant focal seizures
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Korshunov A, et al. Molecular characterization of anaplastic ganglioglioma. Acta Neuropathol. 2019.
